title: 65 Years of Spacesuit Evolution: Silver to Moon Armor
description:
Explore 65 years of spacesuit evolution, from rigid silver cocoons in 1961 to high-tech Artemis moon armor built for deep space.

In 1961, early NASA suits locked rigid under vacuum pressure, forcing astronauts to fight every movement. By 1969, Apollo’s 21-layer armor protected against micrometeorites, yet fabric torsos still forced moonwalkers to bunny-hop.

Today, Artemis suits replace stiff fabric with smooth metal joint bearings and rear-entry hatches, allowing astronauts to twist and kneel effortlessly in lunar dust.

▶️ Watch more Proof of Wonder Shorts: https://www.youtube.com/@proofofwonderscience/shorts

Which spacesuit design surprised you the most—Gemini's golden tether or Artemis's metal joints?

• NASA Johnson Space Center — Apollo A7L / A7LB Lunar Extravehicular Mobility Unit (21 layers, Beta-cloth, Mylar/ballistic micrometeoroid defense, LEVA gold visor, LCVG water-cooling garment & PLSS). — https://www.nasa.gov/history/alsj/
• NASA Johnson Space Center — Space Shuttle Hard Upper Torso EMU & Manned Maneuvering Unit (STS-41B, Bruce McCandless, Feb 7, 1984, 24 nitrogen thrusters, ~100 m untethered) and Artemis Next-Generation Lunar Spacesuits (rear-entry hatch, rotary bearings & lunar regolith dust mitigation, 2026). — https://www.nasa.gov/humans-in-space/spacesuits/
